record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space, viewed as an additive topological group, have a quotient group whose underlying topological space is homeomorphic to the countable product R^omega of real lines?

evidence.quote: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a quotient group which is homeomorphic to R^omega?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space, regarded as an additive topological group with its norm topology. Let $\mathbb{R}^{\omega}$ denote the countable infinite product of copies of the real line, equipped with the product topology. Does there exist a closed subgroup $H \le X$ such that the quotient topological group $X/H$ is homeomorphic (as a topological space) to $\mathbb{R}^{\omega}$?
artifact.category_tag: Topological groups and Banach space quotients
artifact.status_search_result: This question appears as an open problem in the recent survey on separability of topological groups. Related work (e.g., the topological-group separable quotient results showing every Banach space has the tubby torus T^ω as a quotient group) and the long-standing Banach–Mazur separable quotient problem indicate this specific question about an R^ω quotient remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on separability of topological groups, including the question on Banach-space quotients homeomorphic to R^omega.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: The Separable Quotient Problem for Topological Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Every infinite-dimensional Banach space has the tubby torus T^ω as a quotient topological group; related quotient-existence questions are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist but do not resolve the R^omega quotient question.
